standard.title: Reflect to inform practice
standard.description: reflect on their own and others' music to inform choices they make as composers and performers about how they will manipulate elements of music and/or compositional devices
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can develop listening/aural skills and skills for manipulating elements of music to achieve expressive effects when composing, singing and playing instruments (AC9AMU6D01). They have not yet focused explicitly on evaluative reflection — using aural analysis of self and others to drive deliberate choices as a composer or performer.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on their own and others' music using aural skills and music terminology to evaluate how elements of music and compositional devices are used, and use this reflection to inform deliberate choices in their own composing and performing.

nodes.label: Describing music using terminology
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and describe technical and expressive elements of music in their own and others' work using music terminology
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two technical or expressive elements heard in a piece of music using appropriate terminology (e.g. chord progression, phrasing, dynamics, articulation)
nodes.typical_width: Describe multiple technical and expressive elements accurately; use terminology consistently; connect observed elements to their expressive effect
wider: Analyse how a performer interprets or shapes melodies, phrasing or dynamics in a recording — use specific terminology to describe the choices made and evaluate their effect
Compare descriptions of the same piece written by different listeners — identify where terminology is shared and where subjective interpretation diverges

response_modes.reason: Accurate use of music terminology is a precision skill requiring repeated practice. Students need to build fluency with terminology through frequent description tasks across a variety of music before the language becomes a reliable tool for reflection.

success_criteria: Uses at least two music terminology terms accurately to describe a piece
Connects the described element to its expressive effect

nodes.label: Evaluating using focused listening
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use focused listening and selected aural skills to evaluate how elements of music are used, with the purpose of informing their own interpretive decisions
nodes.minimum_width: Listen to a recording with a specific evaluative focus; identify at least one element or device and explain how the performer or composer has used it; connect the observation to a decision about their own work
nodes.typical_width: Apply multiple focused listening strategies to evaluate a recording; use the evaluation to identify specific choices to apply or adapt in their own composing or performing
wider: Use focused listening to evaluate alternative interpretations of a piece (two different recordings) — identify which interpretive choices are more effective for the intended stylistic effect and explain why
Evaluate a recording of their own performance using the same criteria applied to others — identify at least one choice they would change and explain the musical reasoning

response_modes.reason: Evaluation without a clear purpose easily becomes description — students listen and notice things but don't connect observations to decisions. Scaffolding the evaluative reasoning explicitly (what am I listening for → what do I observe → what does this suggest I should do in my own work) keeps reflection purposeful and productive.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Self-evaluation against the same criteria applied to others is a genuinely rich extension — students who extend here are developing metacognitive musical awareness that is meaningfully more demanding than evaluating external recordings alone.
success_criteria: Evaluates at least one element or device in a recording with a stated purpose
Connects the evaluation to at least one decision about their own work

nodes.label: Using ensemble cues in performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use aural and visual cues when playing or singing in an ensemble to maintain ensemble cohesion and respond to musical signals
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one aural cue (e.g. a chord or phrase indicating place in structure) and one visual cue (e.g. a gesture indicating tempo or an entry) used in ensemble performance
nodes.typical_width: Use both aural and visual cues in ensemble performance to maintain place in the structure and respond to other musicians; explain how cue-reading contributes to ensemble cohesion
wider: Reflect on an ensemble rehearsal or performance to identify moments where ensemble cohesion broke down — diagnose whether the cause was missing an aural cue, a visual cue, or a misunderstanding of structure
Limited width — ensemble cue-reading is fundamentally a practised perceptual skill; breadth of ensemble contexts matters more than analytical extension.

response_modes.reason: Ensemble cue-reading is a real-time perceptual skill that improves through practice, not through conceptual variety. Students need repeated ensemble experience to develop the ear-body-response loop that makes cue-reading automatic.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one aural and one visual cue relevant to ensemble performance
Can describe how each cue supports ensemble coordination

nodes.label: Reflection informing compositional and performance choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use reflection on their own and others' music to make deliberate, informed choices as a composer or performer about how to manipulate elements of music or use compositional devices
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one choice made in their own composing or performing that was directly informed by reflection on music (own or others'); explain the connection between what they heard and what they decided
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate a consistent reflective practice in which observations about music (own and others') lead to deliberate compositional or performance choices; document the reflection-to-decision chain
wider: Develop a structured reflection process used across both composition and performance work — compare how reflection functions differently in each context (retrospective in composition, anticipatory and real-time in performance)

Use aural reflection to identify a pattern in their own musical tendencies (e.g. always choosing the same dynamic range, defaulting to similar rhythmic patterns) and deliberately experiment with alternatives

response_modes.reason: This node integrates terminology, focused listening, and ensemble awareness into a deliberate reflective practice that feeds back into making. The coordination of reflection and decision-making as a unified practice — rather than separate activities — is the learning.

The reflection-to-decision chain needs explicit scaffolding — students often reflect and then make their next choice without connecting the two. Structuring the reasoning (what I heard → what it tells me → what I will do differently) makes the feedback loop visible and habitual.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The pattern-identification direction (noticing tendencies in own musical choices and deliberately experimenting with alternatives) is genuinely rich — it develops musical self-awareness and creative range meaningfully beyond minimum.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one deliberate compositional or performance choice that was informed by reflection
Can explain the connection between the reflection and the decision
